messages.subject: Help with shuttle simulation
parts:
Hello,

I'm having some trouble to simulate one step of my process. My current simulation looks like this:

package<- trajectory("Package transport") %>%
  
  ##FLT Loading
  #log_("Transporting")%>%
  seize("FLT_Loading",1)%>%
  timeout(function() rexp(1, 1/FLT_LoadingTime))%>%
  release("FLT_Loading",1)%>%

  #Shuttle
  batch(20, timeout=40, permanent=F)%>%
  #log_("Shuttle")%>%
  seize("Shuttle",1)%>%
  timeout(function() rexp(1, 1/ShuttleTime))%>%
  release("Shuttle",1)

  #Shuttles go to 3 warehouses...

In this code a shuttle is batched and released at every 20 packages that arrives. But in the real process, multiple shuttles, say 10, are being filled until it completes 20 packages. After the loading is complete, there are 4 available drivers to take 4 of them to the warehouses. The other shuttles, even if loaded, have to wait for a driver to come back. I want to how I can put these multiple shuttles at the simulation. I could consider them as new resources, with a capacity of 20, but still I have the problem to simulate that they are transported in batches. There is also a question with the time the empty shuttle takes to come back from the warehouse, while the packages continue their trajectories. Any idea?

Thanks,

That's interesting: it would be a delayed release. I would not only
seize the shuttle(s), but also decrement its capacity by one. Then,
right before releasing it, I would activate a generator to put an
arrival into another trajectory which would spend some time (the time
it takes for the empty shuttle to come back) and then increase the
capacity by one. Schematically:

- batch 20
- seize shuttle
- set capacity shuttle -1
- seize driver
- timeout (to warehouses)
- release driver
- activate generator into other trajectory
- release shuttle
- separate
- ...

And in the other trajectory:

- timeout (shuttle coming back)
- set capacity shuttle +1

What do you think?

  seize(.,"Shuttle",1)%>%

All activities need a trajectory as a first argument. This:

trajectory() %>%
seize("resource", 1)

is equivalent to this:

seize(trajectory(), "resource", 1)

The first option is more convenient, especially when a trajectory has
more than one activity. You don't need the dot, because the pipe (%>%)
places the left-hand side as first argument of the right-hand side.
You only need the pipe if you want to place the left-hand side in a
different position. For instance, this is not the best example, but
you may write

data.frame(x=1:10, y=1:10) %>%
lm(y~x, data = .)

x<-get_mon_arrivals(env,per_resource=TRUE)%>%
  tidyr::spread(resource,start_time)
y<-filter(get_mon_arrivals(env),finished==T)

left_join(x,y,by="name")%>%
  group_by(name)%>%
  filter(finished==T)%>%
  summarise(total_time=max(Driver_Shuttle,na.rm=T)-max(start_time,na.rm=T))
